verdict.rationale: Make documents several headless, programmatic ways to drive automation: a token-authenticated REST API, a TypeScript SDK, webhooks that trigger scenario execution from external services, and an MCP server exposing scenario run and management tools. None of the evidence shows a CLI or CI-pipeline integration, and the API docs never explicitly show running a scenario through the REST API (only AI Agents endpoints, in open beta, mention 'run'). Missing for 10: a documented CLI or CI integration (e.g., a GitHub Action or pipeline guide), explicit REST endpoint docs for running scenarios, and independent or hands-on corroboration of headless/CI use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: All requests to the Make API require authentication with the user authentication token with the relevant scopes enabled.
The Make Typescript SDK provides full support for type definitions and a majority of Make API endpoints, built-in error handling, and response typing.
webhooks create a url that you can call from an external app or service, or from another use webhooks to trigger the execution
Make MCP server allows AI systems, such as large language models (LLMs), to run scenarios and manage the contents of your Make account.
The following endpoints allow you to get, create, update, delete, and run AI Agents. These endpoints are available in **open beta** to all users.
